title: Guard paid generation routes against cross-site POSTs
body:
## Summary
POST /api/leonardo and POST /api/visual-gen/style-dna start paid or metered provider work with no operator guard.

## Description
src/app/api/leonardo/route.ts POST spends Leonardo credit and src/app/api/visual-gen/style-dna/route.ts POST starts a vision job, and neither calls requireOperator, although src/app/api/visual-gen/chaos-cloth/route.ts does. The handlers ignore Content-Type, so a text/plain cross-site form POST avoids a CORS preflight and still parses. Fixed looks like the guard on both, with the in-app callers proven to work when POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN is set: requireOperator demands the token from every call in that mode, and the Material Lab and Style DNA panels send none.

## Flow
- A page on another origin POSTs text/plain JSON to /api/leonardo
- request.json() parses it and generateImage spends a credit
- Build: add requireOperator to both, then settle how same-origin UI calls behave in token mode

## Expected impact
A drive-by page can no longer spend credit on a running dev server. Could break the panels on a machine with POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN set.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - cross-site requests cannot spend provider credit
Before: Read: 0 of the 2 paid POST handlers call requireOperator; chaos-cloth does. Not exercised with a live credit.
After: Predicted 2 of 2 refuse a cross-origin POST with 403.
Method: simulation - no live provider call is allowed in this round, and the token-mode UI behaviour needs a browser run.
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: src/app/api/leonardo/route.ts POST; src/app/api/visual-gen/style-dna/route.ts POST; src/lib/api-auth.ts requireOperator (token mode requires the token on every call)
impact: A drive-by page can no longer spend credit on a running dev server. Could break the panels on a machine with POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN set.
instrument: Route test: cross-origin text/plain POST gives 403 and no provider call; panel e2e with POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN set shows whether UI calls survive.

title: Escape values in buildClothGraphPython itself
body:
## Summary
The cloth script builder interpolates every option into single-quoted Python with no escaping; only the HTTP route now checks them.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/chaos-cloth.ts buildClothGraphPython writes garmentGlbPath, dest, names, mesh paths and transferMethod straight into quoted Python literals. Commit 19741a15c refuses unsafe values at the route, which is the only runtime caller today (character-pipeline.ts only names it in comments and law text). The builder is exported and a future caller inherits the gap. Fixed looks like one Python string-literal escaper applied to every interpolation. The file belongs to another context, so it is out of scope for this round.

## Flow
- A new caller passes a name containing a quote to attachClothToCharacter
- The generated Python breaks or runs the remainder as code
- Build: add an escaper, apply it at all interpolations, test with a quoted value

## Expected impact
Closes the same hole for non-route callers. A wrong escaper could alter a working path, so a builder test must pin ordinary paths unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no caller can inject editor Python through cloth options
Before: 9 option values interpolated unescaped in buildClothGraphPython.
After: Predicted 0 unescaped interpolations.
Method: simulation - the file is outside this round's paths, so the change was not applied.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/chaos-cloth.ts buildClothGraphPython: _task.filename, _garment, create_asset names, SkeletalMesh, PhysicsAsset, TransferMethod lines
impact: Closes the same hole for non-route callers. A wrong escaper could alter a working path, so a builder test must pin ordinary paths unchanged.
instrument: Unit test on buildClothGraphPython: a quoted value stays inside its literal (parse the output with python -c compile), ordinary paths byte-identical.

title: Decide which directories linear-prop outDir may write to
body:
## Summary
POST /api/visual-gen/linear-prop creates and writes into any directory named by outDir.

## Description
src/app/api/visual-gen/linear-prop/route.ts passes outDir to mkdirSync and writeFileSync with no containment. Commit 34685f2c6 added requireOperator, which stops cross-site browsers but deliberately admits header-less local callers. The file name is slugged, but the directory is free. The existing tests write to an OS temp directory, and no in-tree client sends outDir, so the allowed roots are a product decision: drop the field, or restrict it to generated/ and the UE project.

## Flow
- A header-less local caller posts outDir pointing anywhere
- mkdirSync creates it and an .obj is written there
- Decide the allowed roots, then enforce them with a containment check

## Expected impact
Bounds where this route can write. Narrowing it could break an out-of-tree script that passes outDir.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the route writes only inside declared roots
Before: Any absolute path is accepted (the route tests write to OS temp).
After: Depends on the roots chosen.
Method: simulation - the figure depends on a policy nobody has set.
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
impact: Bounds where this route can write. Narrowing it could break an out-of-tree script that passes outDir.

title: Stop blender/detect blocking the event loop on --version
body:
## Summary
GET /api/visual-gen/blender/detect runs execSync with a 10 s timeout on the server event loop, through a shell.

## Description
src/app/api/visual-gen/blender/detect/route.ts:7 calls execSync(`"${path}" --version`, { timeout: 10000 }). While Blender starts, every other request on the single Node process waits, up to 10 s. The path can come from POF_BLENDER and is run through a shell. Fixed looks like an async execFile with no shell. The route test mocks execSync, so it must move with the change.

## Flow
- A panel calls GET blender/detect
- execSync blocks the process for the Blender start time
- Build: promisified execFile, update the test mock, measure event-loop delay on both

## Expected impact
Concurrent requests stop stalling during detection. A mocked-process test has to change with it.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - detection does not stall other requests
Before: Read: 1 synchronous spawn, ceiling 10000 ms. Real blocking time not timed.
After: Predicted 0 ms of event-loop block from the spawn.
Method: simulation - timing needs a real Blender launch, which this round did not run.
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Concurrent requests stop stalling during detection. A mocked-process test has to change with it.
instrument: perf_hooks monitorEventLoopDelay around GET with a stub binary that sleeps 2 s, sync vs async.
